kind: utility judgment, proposed to the operator
gradeScope: confirmed means worth keeping at the stated bounded function; it is not a truth grade for every row or a landing ruling
rankingRule: research and consumer value across the requested arrows, tempered by evidence burden; the first six are the selected pilot families, not a scalar confidence ordering

verdicts.name: Scoped hypothesis predicates
verdicts.reason: C02 evaluates sixteen explicit guards and preserves unknowns. Keep a small source-applicability mechanism; arbitrary predicate inference and full theorem applicability remain open.
verdicts.dayOneReader: compose.mjs needs an obligation environment; Formalization reads unresolved goals
verdicts.receiptRule: Receipt every predicate and its scope in a complete theorem or stated source rule
verdicts.cost: 1 to 6 obligations per claim; a small decidable fragment is checkable; no automatic corpus backfill

verdicts.name: Intertwining rules
verdicts.reason: C23 distinguishes convolution domains, multiplication order and normalization. A narrow equation with conditions directly serves route use; broad analytic rules still need their own evidence.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP intertwinings/routes adapter; Formalization transform intake
verdicts.receiptRule: Quote the full equation and its hypotheses, including boundary terms
verdicts.cost: 2 to 10 rules per transform; exact finite checks useful, infinite rules proof-heavy

verdicts.name: Restricted inverse relations
verdicts.reason: C15 finds reverse routes in bounded fixtures and refuses poles/scaling errors. Universal inverse laws and a production route reader remain owed.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP related/routes adapter; compose currently ignores entry relations
verdicts.receiptRule: Both inverse laws, valid domains and convention conversion, with separate receipts
verdicts.cost: One edge per pair/direction, 15 to 40 pilot rows; finite checks partial; proof debt explicit

verdicts.name: Realization envelopes
verdicts.reason: C30 preserves sixteen static platform claims and detects drift. Code, proof, model and empirical variants were not piloted and cannot share one assurance rule by assumption.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Research_OS bindings.json migration adapter; platform display can read immediately with adapter
verdicts.receiptRule: Immutable artifact/source hash, symbol, contract fingerprint, check result and its scope
verdicts.cost: One row per realization, reuse 90 platform rows; source checks cheap, behavioral proofs rare

verdicts.name: Representation translations and losses
verdicts.reason: C33 identifies nine incomplete information round trips and a normalization ambiguity. Alignment annotations are generated judgments; English meaning preservation is unproved.
verdicts.arrows: M>C; C>M; M>L; L>M; C>L; L>C; atlas
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP get_entry and Research_OS mapread need a translation projection; pilot compares loss
verdicts.receiptRule: Receipted definitions and aligned sentences on both sides; per-guarantee witnesses
verdicts.cost: 2 to 6 arrows per operation; alignment review high; unknown loss never zero

verdicts.name: Atlas transitions
verdicts.reason: C53 checks eight of twenty bounded views, while loss and missing witnesses block twelve. General transitions need carrier, domain, equality and evidence beyond cluster membership.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Disposable transition checker; future MCP atlas reader requires implementation
verdicts.receiptRule: Both definitions, inverse/transport laws and predicate-domain witnesses
verdicts.cost: One arrow per useful overlap; finite models checkable, general proofs high cost

verdicts.name: Atomic claim records
verdicts.reason: The strict reading downgrades compound fields when only some parts are quoted. C02/C23 use specific claim scopes; field-wide grades need this finer target before expansion.
verdicts.dayOneReader: evidence.mjs would need a claim-id lookup; current audit can display spans
verdicts.receiptRule: A window stating the complete proposition, or a pinned theorem plus reviewed interpretation
verdicts.cost: 2 to 8 rows per entry; high semantic review; unsplit compounds remain unchecked

verdicts.name: Convention profiles
verdicts.reason: DFT/Walsh scale and Mobius order controls change results with matching carriers. C33 exposes a real ambiguous recurrence. Name the convention at each representation boundary.
verdicts.dayOneReader: formal.mjs and MCP need convention ids; pilot checks normalization
verdicts.receiptRule: Quote definitions on both sides and the explicit conversion
verdicts.cost: One profile per representation and arrows between profiles; cheap finite checks

verdicts.name: Contract fingerprints
verdicts.reason: C30 detects input/vocabulary drift without moving on evidence-only changes. Its whole-vocabulary dependency overinvalidates, and foreign definition closure is untested.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Research_OS bindings adapter and formal freshness can compare
verdicts.receiptRule: Deterministic digest specification and dependency closure; source pin retained
verdicts.cost: One digest per entry; near-zero claim debt, scope/version review needed

verdicts.name: Named operands and lifetimes
verdicts.reason: The Phone freeze and Research_OS stress reading need persistent principal/authority identity. C02 facts name operands, but a full unification/resource-frame system was not piloted.
verdicts.dayOneReader: compose.mjs requires a named environment; Phone freeze is first case
verdicts.receiptRule: Pinned contract and binding statement for each role; equality witness for aliasing
verdicts.cost: 2 to 5 roles per operation; syntactic joins cheap; identity evidence adds debt

verdicts.name: Invariant temporal scope
verdicts.reason: The consumer reports a step fact carried beyond its step. A scope field needs an explicit propagation rule and relational controls, not a bulk class rename.
verdicts.dayOneReader: compose.mjs already reads classes; would need scope-sensitive propagation
verdicts.receiptRule: Contract/theorem states scope; tests exercise expiration and restoration
verdicts.cost: One scope per claim; cheap metadata; checker semantics need scrutiny

verdicts.name: Claim-targeted counterexamples
verdicts.reason: Zero-divisor, pole, normalization and graphic-forgetting witnesses explain precise failures. Retain the attacked claim and domain so examples cannot refute unrelated statements.
verdicts.dayOneReader: misalign/audit display and pilot evaluator can read; route checker needs hookup
verdicts.receiptRule: Exact object and evaluation or formal negation, tied to a claim id
verdicts.cost: 1 to 5 cases per disputed claim; often cheap to execute; semantics still reviewed

verdicts.name: Dependent result domains
verdicts.reason: Inverse validity depends on the produced range; the Mobius pole and quadratic overlap make this concrete. Analytic convergence-region inference still needs proofs.
verdicts.dayOneReader: compose.mjs needs dependent result facts; transform routes first
verdicts.receiptRule: Theorem giving the dependency, including boundary conditions
verdicts.cost: 1 to 3 rows per transform; interval algebra cheap, analytic facts hard

verdicts.name: External proof links
verdicts.reason: Research_OS and Formalization already hold relevant theorems externally. A pinned declaration plus reviewed statement/definition/axiom correspondence is needed before local evidence can read it.
verdicts.dayOneReader: lean.mjs/evidence.mjs need an external-project adapter
verdicts.receiptRule: Pinned theorem source plus replay log and reviewed statement comparison
verdicts.cost: One row per theorem mapping; kernel runs costly; imported standing remains local

verdicts.name: Reviewed operation identity
verdicts.reason: The consumers work around duplicate anchors, and domain views recur in pilots. Same names, matching finite cases and similar signatures cannot settle canonical identity.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Research_OS mapread/decompose needs canonical ids
verdicts.receiptRule: Definitional equality or reviewed equivalence at stated granularity; never name alone
verdicts.cost: One mapping per duplicate view; cheap indexing, expensive adjudication

verdicts.name: Stored whole-chain proofs
verdicts.reason: compose already accepts a per-call proof citation. Persistence helps only if chain, model, policy, operand identities and axioms are bound precisely enough to prevent reuse on a different claim.
verdicts.dayOneReader: compose.mjs already accepts per-call proofs; needs scoped store adapter
verdicts.receiptRule: External theorem, reviewed model correspondence and exact chain fingerprint
verdicts.cost: One row per proof/policy/chain version; modest indexing, high alignment cost

verdicts.name: Operator laws
verdicts.reason: C23's derivative, evaluation and transpose laws act on operators rather than on input invariants. Distinct law kinds prevent the preserved/broken misfiling seen by intake.
verdicts.dayOneReader: compose.mjs needs law-kind handling; Formalization can use laws
verdicts.receiptRule: Complete law theorem with quantifiers and hypotheses
verdicts.cost: 1 to 5 rows per operator; some algebraic laws executable; rest need proofs

verdicts.name: Executable semantic models
verdicts.reason: The code arrow needs integer, crash, effect and runtime semantics. Finite pilot models and proposition erasure show the boundary; no deployment refinement proof was run.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Guardians export and D9 compose need model references
verdicts.receiptRule: Pinned executable and semantic model, refinement argument and test boundary
verdicts.cost: One model per runtime/API family plus bindings; large proof debt

verdicts.name: Quantitative guarantees
verdicts.reason: Intake reports bounds and probabilities in prose. Typed parameters would enable goal constraints, but a formula field or units conversion does not discharge a probabilistic theorem.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP problem query and compose would need quantity constraints
verdicts.receiptRule: Quote the complete bound with hypotheses, constants/conventions and probability space
verdicts.cost: 1 to 4 bound rows per relevant claim; algebra partly decidable; many theorem-specific gaps

verdicts.name: Foundational profiles
verdicts.reason: Lean audits axiom dependencies and consumer proof admission is foundation-sensitive. Store explicit assumptions separately from proof correctness and statement fidelity.
verdicts.dayOneReader: lean.mjs and external-proof adapter need axiom-set comparison
verdicts.receiptRule: Kernel axiom audit at a pin plus statement-fidelity review
verdicts.cost: One audit per proof artifact; mechanical extraction, semantic alignment debt

verdicts.name: Statement/definition fingerprints
verdicts.reason: Name-stable changes can alter a proof's referent. Exact bytes are useful identity evidence, while canonical semantic hashing and definition closure remain unestablished here.
verdicts.dayOneReader: formal.mjs freshness and Research_OS ingest can compare
verdicts.receiptRule: Canonicalization algorithm/version, source hash and collision/normalization tests
verdicts.cost: One digest per declaration/definition closure; cheap hashes after extraction

verdicts.name: Dependency invalidation
verdicts.reason: The atlas paper requires regional updates on overlaps and C30 detects conservative dependency drift. A precise sparse dependency graph needs mutation coverage beyond this pilot.
verdicts.dayOneReader: build/evidence and future atlas adapter need dependency edges
verdicts.receiptRule: Each dependency is pinned; mutation controls show exact affected set
verdicts.cost: 1 to 10 dependencies per claim; graph traversal cheap, missing edges costly

verdicts.name: Consumer field-use manifests
verdicts.reason: mapread drops declared typing, conditions and relation metadata. A pinned projection/conformance declaration makes the day-one reader testable instead of assuming exported means consumed.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Research_OS mapread and MCP tool server could publish capabilities
verdicts.receiptRule: Pinned parser/consumer source and executable conformance fixture
verdicts.cost: One profile per consumer version; cheap structural checks

verdicts.name: Postconditions and read-back results
verdicts.reason: Typed.java infers some successes from absent matching output. Distinguishing command error from a checked negative observation is useful; this survey ran no Android action.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Phone Typed.java adapter is first reader
verdicts.receiptRule: Pinned predicate and read-back program, exit/status semantics and probe tests
verdicts.cost: One spec per action variant; finite negative controls cheap; device coverage owed

verdicts.name: Independent observation ledger
verdicts.reason: The operator's rule and consumer event shape are present. Build applicability, observer independence, repetitions and the crossing of assurance ladders need a dedicated device pilot.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Phone Observe adapter and assurance reducer need mapping
verdicts.receiptRule: Hashed log, probe build, repeat ids and observer independence; instance data excluded
verdicts.cost: Two or more runs per claim/build; expensive device access; readings stay readings

verdicts.name: Verification tasks and checker prerequisites
verdicts.reason: The kit already makes check assumptions explicit; evidence queues need comparable task identities. A recorded passing run grants only its own scoped utility claim.
verdicts.dayOneReader: evidence.mjs and Formalization queue need task ids
verdicts.receiptRule: Hashed checker/input/output, declared checker prerequisites and assumption list
verdicts.cost: One task per obligation/run; runnable checks cheap; external checks may be expensive

verdicts.name: Entry nature and operation shape
verdicts.reason: Intake classifies non-operations and dependent or nonunique outputs. A small reviewed distinction helps; a universal shape vocabulary would multiply classification debt.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP search needs nature filters; compose must reject unsupported shapes
verdicts.receiptRule: Receipt a defining statement that identifies the shape, separate from the legacy kind
verdicts.cost: One record per reviewed home; easy syntax, moderate classification debt

verdicts.name: Implementation/refinement edges
verdicts.reason: FFT/DFT already distinguish algorithm from operation, while bounded numeric equality is weaker than refinement. Keep cost/error on the realization and its bridge.
verdicts.dayOneReader: export-guardians.mjs and realization adapter would read
verdicts.receiptRule: Correctness/refinement theorem or bounded executable validation
verdicts.cost: One or more edges per implementation; refinement proofs costly

verdicts.name: Composite DAG recipes
verdicts.reason: Useful routes need joint operands and missing-step obligations. Existing straight-line compose is a starting reader; full DAG and external-resource semantics remain extra work.
verdicts.dayOneReader: compose.mjs needs a DAG frontend; MCP can display expanded routes
verdicts.receiptRule: Receipt each step and its join, with whole-recipe obligations
verdicts.cost: 3 to 20 step references per route; syntax easy, coverage limited by nodes

verdicts.name: Typed uses/problem classes
verdicts.reason: Intake's routes can miss the useful rule even when the entry exists. Goal-conditioned retrieval merits a small benchmark after rules and applicability are explicit.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP routes adapter; Formalization proof queue can reuse goals
verdicts.receiptRule: Receipted solved instance or theorem, with reusable applicability conditions
verdicts.cost: 1 to 5 uses per operation; evidence-heavy; task names alone add debt

verdicts.name: Obstruction theorems
verdicts.reason: The atlas needs route-pruning knowledge. Add a verified obstruction when a real route needs it; neither a failed search nor a missing inverse field establishes impossibility.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP routes and Formalization queue need obstruction queries
verdicts.receiptRule: Counterexample or impossibility theorem with exactly stated scope
verdicts.cost: 1 to 3 rows per blocked goal; proof-heavy, high pruning value

verdicts.name: Lost information and inverse obstructions
verdicts.reason: C53's graphic map forgets isolated vertices and C15 needs image restrictions. Kernel/fiber accounts are valuable when their objects and lost laws are actually specified.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Inverse-route adapter and Formalization can use
verdicts.receiptRule: Kernel/fiber theorem, explicit collision or noninjectivity witness
verdicts.cost: One row per lossy transform; finite collisions easy; general fibers hard

verdicts.name: Axiom dependency/discharge graph
verdicts.reason: Axiom extraction exists in Lean. Cross-library identity, discharge and retraction propagation add obligations beyond extracting a dependency list.
verdicts.dayOneReader: lean.mjs and Formalization can export closure; atlas reader needed
verdicts.receiptRule: Kernel dependency extraction plus axiom identity and discharge theorem
verdicts.cost: Potentially many edges; extraction cheap after build; semantic equivalence reviewed

verdicts.name: Round-trip certificates
verdicts.reason: C15 and C53 verify finite loops, and C33 verifies no language equivalence. Every certificate must state its equality level, domain and stronger proof still owed.
verdicts.dayOneReader: formal.mjs adapter and disposable round-trip checker
verdicts.receiptRule: Both arrows, domain, equality notion and proof/finite test at named scope
verdicts.cost: One certificate per loop; finite tests cheap, semantic equivalence expensive

verdicts.name: Executable atlas charts
verdicts.reason: The paper's charts are consistent relational views over one library. A small projection with shared ids is a tractable first form; an atlas runtime is absent.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP/chart exporter would need an adapter; no atlas runtime exists
verdicts.receiptRule: Pinned view definition and membership/dependency receipts
verdicts.cost: One view plus membership rows; cheap projection, semantic chart choice reviewed

verdicts.name: Explicit overlaps
verdicts.reason: The pilots require positivity, fixed-point restrictions or fixed bases. Mere shared members do not identify a valid overlap or settle its claim correspondence.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Future chart validator; pilot overlap checker first
verdicts.receiptRule: Membership on both sides and reviewed equivalence of shared claims
verdicts.cost: One overlap per neighboring chart pair; potentially quadratic, use sparse overlaps

verdicts.name: Cocycle/coherence evidence
verdicts.reason: A wrong quadratic factor is caught around one finite cycle. Global coherence requires a generating presentation and the right equality/natural-isomorphism witnesses.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Disposable cycle checker first; no present script checks atlas cycles
verdicts.receiptRule: Transition-domain intersection plus equality/natural-isomorphism witness
verdicts.cost: Cycles grow rapidly; verify generators rather than enumerate all; high proof debt

verdicts.name: Analogy degradation and residuals
verdicts.reason: C53 retains lossy graphic abstraction and unknown comparison rows without promoting them to isomorphisms. Ontology alignment confidence cannot replace this lost-law account.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP related display and transition checker need residual grades
verdicts.receiptRule: Counterexample or failed transport law and exact retained structure
verdicts.cost: One row per bridge boundary; bounded tests useful; analogy judgment persists

verdicts.name: Local retyping of imports
verdicts.reason: The paper explicitly keeps imported standing local, while MMT supports theory interpretation. A receiver must still check the intended statement under its own foundation.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Formalization intake and Research_OS gate would need import envelopes
verdicts.receiptRule: Original provenance plus local challenge/replay under receiving axioms
verdicts.cost: One admission per claim/foundation; expensive but bounded by use

verdicts.name: Regional maintenance and governance
verdicts.reason: The paper scopes recomputation by region/overlap. Sparse dependency work, versioning and authority over region definitions remain separate engineering/governance questions.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Future atlas builder; existing build can prototype an invalidation index
verdicts.receiptRule: Public role/ruling and dependency receipts; replay compares affected set
verdicts.cost: One region record plus sparse edges; low compute, governance review

verdicts.name: Adjoint pairs
verdicts.reason: The nLab gives unit/counit triangle identities as concrete data. A useful map edge must carry side, hom correspondence and hypotheses, rather than an inverse-like label.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Formalization and an MCP related adapter
verdicts.receiptRule: Adjunction statement and unit/counit identities at a source pin
verdicts.cost: One pair plus 2 to 4 law rows; formal transport possible; high semantic review

verdicts.name: Dualities and variance
verdicts.reason: Rocq relation signatures and typed interpretations support directed transport. Finiteness, opposite categories and double-dual restrictions need individual witnesses.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP related adapter and future transport checker
verdicts.receiptRule: Duality theorem with finiteness/reflexivity and variance
verdicts.cost: One edge plus laws per duality; medium/high proof cost

verdicts.name: Specialization/generalization
verdicts.reason: Theory interpretations offer a rigorous form. A reviewed substitution and premise implication can extend formal match grading without claiming that naming a parent proves entailment.
verdicts.dayOneReader: formal.mjs match grading and MCP relation search need witness fields
verdicts.receiptRule: The general theorem plus checked substitution and premise entailment
verdicts.cost: One edge per useful specialization; some substitutions cheap; long-tail debt

verdicts.name: Universal specifications
verdicts.reason: Adjunction and theory-morphism precedents support structured specifications. Start with a construction a consumer needs; existence and uniqueness must both be receipted.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Formalization intake and MCP require a universal-property query
verdicts.receiptRule: Pinned universal statement including existence and uniqueness, not the word universal
verdicts.cost: One structured property per construction; proof-heavy; imported obligations explicit

verdicts.name: Continuum/discrete convergence bridges
verdicts.reason: Encoding conversion has precedents, but convergence topology, stability and rates do not follow. No such theorem was verified by these finite pilots.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP routes and future numeric adapter
verdicts.receiptRule: Convergence theorem with norm/topology, mesh and stability assumptions
verdicts.cost: Several rows per method; analytic proofs expensive; likely small coverage

verdicts.name: Families and degenerations
verdicts.reason: A parameter field alone cannot say what survives at a singular limit. The limiting object, topology and lost laws need a small independently checked family.
verdicts.dayOneReader: deform.mjs can consume a family adapter; MCP can browse
verdicts.receiptRule: Source formula and range; certificate or computed limiting identity
verdicts.cost: One family plus member links; symbolic limits mixed; many new unchecked limits

verdicts.name: Branches, repeats and hyperproperties
verdicts.reason: The redirect note needs bounded repetition and compose already separates hyperproperties. Extending a straight-line grammar without proof rules would introduce false preservation claims.
verdicts.dayOneReader: compose.mjs/Guardians adapter would need control-flow IR
verdicts.receiptRule: Loop invariant/variant, branch guards and route-specific source receipts
verdicts.cost: Many obligations per program; verification expensive; do not unfold indefinitely

verdicts.name: Reproducible worked instances
verdicts.reason: All six pilots use exact or bounded fixtures to expose conventions and failures. Keep a few per consumed rule with the source/fixture distinction and no universal-proof promotion.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP get_entry can display; a disposable evaluator executes fixtures
verdicts.receiptRule: Source example plus exact recomputation, with invented test inputs labeled
verdicts.cost: 3 to 10 instances per selected entry; finite evaluation cheap; universal claims remain unchecked

verdicts.name: Mathematical standing apart from evidence
verdicts.reason: The uniform legacy status does not distinguish conjecture from unchecked description. A dated claim/foundation status could, but any retirement of existing status is the operator's later decision.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP display and Formalization queue need this separate axis
verdicts.receiptRule: Dated primary statement, named conditions and foundation; revisions stay visible
verdicts.cost: One or more time-indexed rows per claim; ongoing review; folklore remains weak

verdicts.name: Claim provenance, rights and retraction
verdicts.reason: The exact-source newline correction illustrates the need for immutable source identity and correction history. References and source reliability have working precedents; entailment remains a separate review.
verdicts.dayOneReader: catalogue.mjs/evidence.mjs need claim-source edges
verdicts.receiptRule: Immutable source hash, rights, offsets, authorship and dated retraction
verdicts.cost: One source row reused by many claims; legal/semantic checks mixed

verdicts.name: Consumer coverage and evidence debt
verdicts.reason: The survey distinguishes 103 receipt checks from bounded semantics and zero new universal proofs. Recomputable consumer-specific denominators are more useful than another undifferentiated count.
verdicts.dayOneReader: STATUS/build reports and Research_OS gap finder can add dimensions
verdicts.receiptRule: Counts recomputed from pinned inputs, unresolved denominator explicit
verdicts.cost: Aggregate rows derived, no truth debt; interpretation remains a judgment

verdicts.name: Anchor roles and coverage fidelity
verdicts.reason: Research_OS's own readings show broad type anchors overassign inner operations. Role metadata plus independent negative matches may help; higher clean counts alone would not confirm it.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Research_OS decompose/mapread need role metadata
verdicts.receiptRule: Read defining declaration and sampled mappings; independent negative matches
verdicts.cost: One role per link and bounded coverage audit; moderate effort

verdicts.name: Lexicon and symbol senses
verdicts.reason: Wikidata formula-symbol records and ontology alignments offer partial precedents. Overloaded mathematical names still need scoped senses and a retrieval precision check.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP search can consume an alias table; misalign can use reviewed senses
verdicts.receiptRule: Source usage with span/context; ambiguous terms keep alternatives
verdicts.cost: 2 to 10 labels per entry; lots of review; easy to inflate unchecked pile

verdicts.name: Controlled-language parses
verdicts.reason: Statement markup exists, but this search established no verified language-to-claim parser for the map. C33's manual alignments cannot stand in for one.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP authoring/intake adapter would be needed; no present parser
verdicts.receiptRule: Source sentence, explicit parse and formal alignment review
verdicts.cost: One parse per claim; syntactic checks easy, meaning costly

verdicts.name: Proof move skeletons
verdicts.reason: OMDoc can hold structured proofs, but a cross-domain skeleton is a plan with holes. Evaluate on independently fixed goals before storing a large unchecked plan corpus.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP route search and Formalization intake need a planner adapter
verdicts.receiptRule: Worked proof with step alignment; plan is generation until proof checked
verdicts.cost: 5 to 30 moves per proof; annotation expensive; easy unchecked growth

verdicts.name: Open goals and independence
verdicts.reason: Explicit foundation-relative liabilities protect against confusing unknown with false. Independence must cite a result about a named theory, not the absence of a local proof.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Formalization queue and MCP display
verdicts.receiptRule: Primary independence result naming theory, or a dated open obligation with no truth promotion
verdicts.cost: One row per goal/foundation; proof-heavy; unknown stays unchecked

verdicts.name: Dead routes and reopening conditions
verdicts.reason: The atlas's negative record and generation history justify selective retention. The failed domain experiment is a useful record; a timeout can only receipt a bounded attempt.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP route query and generation records need an index
verdicts.receiptRule: Negative experiment log or proved obstruction; search limits are explicit
verdicts.cost: One row per serious attempt; broad failed searches expensive; no impossibility by timeout

verdicts.name: Measurement uncertainty models
verdicts.reason: Provenance and reliability records are precedents, while noise models and error propagation are additional empirical claims. No measurements were taken in this task.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Observation consumer and quantity adapter would be needed
verdicts.receiptRule: Public experimental protocol, calibrated error model and raw-log digest
verdicts.cost: Many observations per method; statistics checkable conditional on model; high review cost

verdicts.name: Phenomenological departure and uncertified compression
verdicts.reason: The paper asks for both, and empirical failure differs from a formal counterexample. Keep demand signals in domain records until the model and observation boundary is specified.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Research_OS record and future atlas use-query
verdicts.receiptRule: Public domain protocol/observations and precise mismatch with model
verdicts.cost: Domain-specific rows and repeated measurements; large empirical debt

verdicts.name: Performance/resource envelopes
verdicts.reason: Useful as attached realization readings when a selector needs them; expensive as a map-wide benchmark layer. These trial wall times are not asymptotic complexity or hardware-independent guarantees.
verdicts.dayOneReader: Realization selector and MCP display would need reader code
verdicts.receiptRule: Reproducible benchmark log with public hardware class, workload and pin
verdicts.cost: Many runs per implementation; environmental drift; readings never standing

verdicts.name: Technique clusters and speculative bridges
verdicts.reason: Useful as proposal/search material, risky as trusted transport metadata. Require demonstrated route value and departure witnesses before bulk cluster membership claims.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP search adapter and generation queue
verdicts.receiptRule: Receipted worked proofs for members; clustering output is a lead
verdicts.cost: Many membership judgments; high unchecked risk; keep suggestions out of standing

verdicts.name: Computed reference/priority atlas
verdicts.reason: The paper separates estimated reference proposals from verified theory edges. This is curatorial infrastructure with substantial corpus/credit costs, not a prerequisite for operation contracts.
verdicts.dayOneReader: catalogue import and future reference-atlas adapter
verdicts.receiptRule: Dated content hashes and typed citation evidence; estimates labeled
verdicts.cost: Potentially dense edges; expensive corpus access and credit review

verdicts.name: Learned search scores
verdicts.reason: Scores can order leads, but no fetched source or pilot demonstrates a gain for this map. Require a held-out relevance test against lexical/identifier retrieval; never change evidence grades.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP search could read optional ranks
verdicts.receiptRule: Pinned scorer, held-out relevance judgments and leakage controls
verdicts.cost: One vector per entry/model; cheap inference, expensive evaluation

verdicts.name: One global truth/utility score
verdicts.reason: It mixes claim truth, preference and usefulness, conceals the weakest premise and cannot preserve consumer-specific applicability. Keep separate grades, evidence and measured readings.
verdicts.dayOneReader: MCP could display; no semantic reader benefits identified
verdicts.receiptRule: Would require justified calibration across unrelated claims and consumers
verdicts.cost: One scalar per entry; cheap storage, costly/possibly incoherent calibration
